title: Patient Registration for Interventional Roadmaps
summary:
The study records how patients lie on the examination table during certain tomographic examinations (e.g., CT, PET/CT, or SPECT/CT—but not MRI). The aim is to make it easier to compare images taken at different times, especially in follow-up examinations of the same person. If the body posture is as consistent as possible and the patient does not move during the examination, fewer image errors occur. In addition, the images are easier to compare, and the diagnosis becomes more reliable.
Additional sensors are used to accurately record body posture during normal scans: a pressure-sensitive mat that is placed under the patient on the table and measures how body pressure is distributed, one or more RGB-D cameras that capture color images (red-green-blue = RGB) and depth information of the body, and optionally a thermal imaging camera that provides additional thermal images to better understand the body position. The measurements only take place while the person is lying on the examination table. This does not interfere with the actual scan.

interventions.name:
Observational study (prospective, non-interventional, single-arm):

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Adult patients (≥ 18 years) with planned CT, PET/CT, or SPECT/CT scans at Augsburg University Hospital.
- The planned tomographic scan includes at least half of the abdomen and/or thorax, ideally also the head.
- A previous CT scan of the abdomen and/or thorax is available.
Exclusion criteria:
- Patients whose previous CT scan did not include the abdomen/thorax region.
- Patients whose upcoming CT, PET/CT, or SPECT/CT scan does not include at least half of the abdomen/thorax.
